# PATHWAYS v3.1: methods (DRAFT; generated by tools/pathways_methods.py, do not edit by hand)

Four pathways for new residential construction in New Zealand, 2026-2050, built from five levers and applied to the frozen baseline (baseline-pb-v3.1, reference replacement scenario S3-10), assessed against the climate-change budgets of the planetary-boundary layer (acquired rights, AR; ability to pay, AtP). The model is unchanged: `pathways.py` re-calls `engine.forward()` with copies of the reference inputs modified by `levers.py` (hooks: outputs/pathways/HOOKS.md); no baseline output is rewritten (tests/test_baseline_lock.py, SHA-256 of every baseline output at tag baseline-PB_v3.1). With every lever off the run reproduces the reference run (maximum relative difference 4.4e-16; tests/test_pathways.py). Table 1: outputs/pathways/LEVERS_TABLE.md.

## Pathways and demand bands

| pathway | levers | demand band targeted |
|---|---|---|
| P1 Right-size space | L1 Right-sized new dwellings | extra space per dwelling and the dwelling size of every non-growth band |
| P2 Occupy the existing stock | L2a Lower vacancy, L2b Near-term surplus absorbed | vacancy allowance (incl. the vacancy change) and the near-term market excess |
| P3 Keep and reuse | L3 Fewer removals | long-run replacement (demolition) and the redevelopment wave |
| P4 Build better | L5 Best-practice materials | carbon per m² (A1-A3) of every band |
| P5 All pathways | all five | all of the above |

**Typology mix (L4 removed).** L4 evaluated in pathways_v2 and removed: within the embodied-carbon scope a denser mix raises A1-A3 per m2 (attached typologies carry more per m2), while its benefits (infrastructure, operational energy, land) are outside the scope. Values from tag pathways_v2 (S3-10): L4 central / stretch carbon -0.39% / -2.94% vs P0 while carbon per m² rose from 240.9 to 241.9 / 248.8 kg CO₂e; its lever Shapley share was 1.7% / 5.8%. The typology shares stay at the baseline held mix in every run (P0-P5 and T).

Growth and house-splitting are untargeted by design: population and household formation are exogenous (as in Pellan et al. 2024). Every run reports floor area and carbon by demand band (Boss definitions; pathways_bands.csv), so the attribution by band is exact and needs no decomposition.

## Conventions

* Ramp (all levers): s(y) = 1 / (1 + exp(−k (y − 2030.5))), k = ln(81)/6 = 0.7324 (s rises from 10% to 90% within 6 years); w(y) = (s(y) − s(2026)) / (s(2035) − s(2026)) for 2026 ≤ y ≤ 2035, w = 1 after 2035, w(2026) = 0. A lever moves a quantity from its baseline b to its target x as b + w(y)(x − b). Basis: full roll-out by 2035 following RECC (Pauliuk et al. 2024, J. Ind. Ecol. 28, 1699: circular-economy strategies fully implemented by 2035). Sensitivities (P5), same k: ramp2030 (midpoint 2028.5, full strength 2030, w(2026) = 0; w(2030) = 1) and ramp2045 (midpoint 2035.5, full strength 2045; the same adoption speed ten years later).
* 2026 is observed (consented floor area fixed) and identical in every run.
* Near-term market excess: frozen at the baseline path, in dwellings, except where L2b absorbs the surplus (it is the observed 2026 pipeline, not demand).
* Accounting as the baseline (time-resolved): within-window carbon = upfront (A1-A5 + soil) in the construction year + replacements & repaints (B2, B4) in 2026-2050; later events and all C1-C4 of the 2026-2050 cohorts are committed after 2050 (range: lower with the 2050 factors held, upper at 2025 factors; `events.committed` with each run's floor area by typology).

## Levers as implemented (levers.py)

    L1   size_t(y) = occ_t(y) + [1 − f w(y)] (size_ref_t − occ_t(y)),   occ_t(y) = S(y) · OLF_t
    L2a  v(y) = v0 + w(y)(v* − v0)
    L2b  join = market_excess(E_nojoin, O26, ρ, 2027, surplus, absorption a)
    L3   demol(y) = demol · (1 − w(y) d);  resid(y) = resid_LR + (resid_S3(y) − resid_LR)(1 − w(y) d)
    L5   A1-A3_t(y) = [1 − w(y)(1 − r)] · (A1-A3_t,2025 − R13_t(y))   (A4-A5, B events, C1-C4, soil unchanged)

S and OLF are the engine's (S = population / households of the median path; OLF per typology from the case studies), so occ_t is the occupied area the engine uses for the growth and extra-space bands. size_ref: realised new-dwelling size, mean of 2023-2025. L1 removes a share f of the extra-space margin (size − S(y) · OLF): full strength in 2035, f held constant to 2050, so the sizes then follow S(y). L1 holds a typology / year at size_ref where size_ref ≤ occ (never binds: 0 typology-years held). L2a acts through the stock identity: while v falls the vacancy-change term releases existing dwellings once (cumulative release in pathways_runs.csv, by year in pathways_annual.csv); under the logistic ramp the release peaks where w rises fastest (2029-2032). R13: the A1-A3 decarbonisation of the baseline (Horup et al. 2025, item level).

### L5: Harrell-Davis estimator

Sample: the 14 independent case studies of the detached and townhouse typologies (duplicates excluded; apartments have one independent case and are not in the sample), 2025 A1-A3 per m² (outputs/factors/factors_building.csv). Scale-free ratio x_i = A1-A3_i / pooled A1-A3 of its typology (pooling as Building_factors.pool; recomputed pooled values equal the model's to 2.8e-14 kg/m²). Harrell & Davis (1982):

    Q̂(q) = Σ_i W_i x_(i),   W_i = I_{i/n}(a, b) − I_{(i−1)/n}(a, b),   a = q(n + 1),   b = (1 − q)(n + 1)

with I the regularised incomplete beta function, implemented directly and checked against scipy.stats.mstats.hdquantiles (≤ 1e-10). Interval: nonparametric bootstrap of the cases, B = 10,000, seed 20261008, percentile 95% (Efron & Tibshirani 1993). The pathway runs use the point estimate; the same r applies to all three typologies (apartments held at r = 1 as a sensitivity).

## Attribution

Shapley values (Shapley 1953; for emissions decompositions Albrecht, François & Schoors 2002) of each player for the reduction v(∅) − v(N):

    φ_i = Σ_{S ⊆ N∖{i}} |S|! (|N| − |S| − 1)! / |N|! · [v(S) − v(S ∪ {i})]

Players: the four pathways P1-P4 (|N| = 4, 16 subsets; main) and the five levers (|N| = 5, 32 subsets; SI); every subset is a full run; v = cumulative within-window carbon (kt) or cumulative LoE AR. Computed in exact rational arithmetic on the run values, so Σ_i φ_i = P0 − P5 exactly (tested).

## AESA gap

Budgets B_AR(t), B_AtP(t) for S3-10 from outputs/pb_annual.csv (no lever changes population). Cumulative LoE = Σ I(t) / Σ B(t) over 2026-2050 (aesa.cumulative_loe); remaining reduction needed = 1 − 1/LoE.

**Back-cast.** I(t; k) = F(t) + k · G(t), F the 2026 cohort (its upfront and in-window events), G the 2027-2050 cohorts; scaling their floor area by k keeps the typology mix and the replacement share, hence the soil share. k solves Σ I(t; k) = Σ B_AR(t) (scipy.optimize.brentq on [0, 1], xtol 1e-15; checked against the closed form). AtP: the minimum attainable cumulative LoE is Σ F / Σ B_AtP (k = 0).

**Solution space** (after Horup et al. 2025, Fig. 6): I(t; d, i) = F(t) + (1 − d)[(1 − i) G_ns(t) + G_soil(t)] on P0. Pathways sit at d = 1 − GFA_P / GFA_0 and i = 1 − (C_P / GFA_P) / (C_0 / GFA_0) (2027-2050 cohorts; C non-soil within the window); a negative i would mean more carbon per m².

## Checks (tests/test_pathways.py, tests/test_baseline_lock.py)

* P0 = reference run (≤ 1e-9 relative): annual carbon, upfront, in-window B, floor area by typology, demand bands, committed range, cumulative LoE AR / AtP; S1 and S2 P0 = the PB scenario runs.
* Each lever at zero strength = the baseline; 2026 identical in every run; lever functions never modify their inputs; the logistic ramp is 0 in 2026, 1 from 2035 and monotone.
* L1 sizes ≥ occupied area S·OLF in every typology, year and run; D ≥ S·OLF (engine extra_clip = 0); implied vacancy ≥ 4.0%; no negative dwellings built.
* Harrell-Davis = scipy.stats.mstats.hdquantiles (≤ 1e-10); pathway and lever Shapley efficiency exact; demand bands add up to the totals; back-cast LoE AR = 1 (≤ 1e-9).
* Baseline outputs: SHA-256 equal to tag baseline-PB_v3.1 (tests/baseline_manifest.json).

## Limitations

* L3 is an upper bound: the carbon of renovating the buildings kept in use is not modelled (Napiontek et al. 2025, Resour. Conserv. Recycl. 215, 108117).
* L5 rests on 14 case studies; the stretch interval is wide (0.61-0.95). The ratio is pooled across detached and townhouses (scale-free) and applied to apartments too (one independent apartment case; held at r = 1 as a sensitivity), and to the pooled A1-A3 of every item: the best-practice material mix is assumed transferable.
* L1 keeps the engine's occupied area (S·OLF) and cuts only the space above it; the occupancy load factor per typology and design rules (minimum room sizes) are not modelled.
* The typology mix is held at the baseline (L4 removed; see above): the infrastructure, operational-energy and land benefits of denser forms are outside the embodied-carbon scope.
* L2a: v0 = 5.39% is the published 2023 empty-dwelling share while the target range (4.01% in 1996 to 5.38% in 2023) is on a consistent definition; targets rounded to 0.1 point; 4.0% is the lowest NZ vacancy rate on that definition. The release of existing dwellings acts once, while the rate falls.
* The near-term excess is frozen in dwellings, so its floor area follows L1 through the blended size.
* Levers are parameter changes on the baseline model; no behavioural, market or rebound response is modelled; interactions are those of the model (attributed by Shapley values).
* The pathways are deterministic (median demographics); the baseline Monte Carlo is not re-run for them. Budgets are static (PB layer limitations apply).
* Omitted: Occupancy / household size (household size is a demographic input of the baseline (Stats NZ household projections, Boss.HH_SIZE_VARIANT) and sets the number of households, not a construction choice; a lever on it needs a behavioural or policy model of household formation that v2 does not have (growth and house-splitting are untargeted by design, as in Pellan et al. 2024)); Brownfield soil (the soil factor is one area-weighted value for Auckland land zoned for urbanisation (Christoforatos, Pickering & Schipper 2026) and soil is already zero on the replacement bands; no national brownfield share is in the inputs to parameterise a shift); Lightweighting (the case studies give A1-A3 per m2 by material and item, not structural mass by design alternative; a mass reduction cannot be separated from the material choice already covered by L5); Bio-based archetypes (no typology has a bio-based archetype among the 16 case studies, and the model's biogenic-carbon convention (timber C1-C4 excludes biogenic CO2) would need extending; overlaps L5).


## Theoretical limit T (PATHWAYS v3.1)

> T is a hyper-optimistic theoretical limit (thought experiment): all assumptions at full strength from 1 January 2027, combining best observed attributes of different buildings and places; not a proposal or a feasible pathway (potentials hierarchy: theoretical > technical > realisable).

**Definition.** T = P5-stretch (no L4) with six overrides at full strength from 1 January 2027 (w = 1 for every lever in 2027-2050, no ramp; 2026 observed and untouched): T1 no idle stock (v = 0; near-term surplus absorbed in full), T2 no extra space (new-dwelling size = occupied area S(t) · OLF), T3 minimum space per person (OLF of every new building = the lowest independent design OLF), T4 best materials (each typology at its own best independent case; apartments held), T5 best soil (lowest soil order), T6 urban densification (a share s of the non-replacement new floor area on previously developed land, zero soil). L3 (−40%) as P5-stretch; the typology shares stay at the baseline held mix. BAU decarbonisation applies in T as in every run (A1-A3 item paths of Horup et al. 2025, A4-A5 e^(-0.01 (t - 2025)); the lift held at 2025 as in the baseline). The potentials hierarchy (theoretical > technical > realisable) places T at the theoretical end; the logistic-ramp T (T-ramp) is an SI sensitivity.

| item | how it works (model terms) | assumption | T value | source (full citation) | tag |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| T1 No idle stock | v = 0 from 2027 (`v`); near-term surplus absorbed in full; banking rule: built_t = max(0, raw_t - bank_(t-1)), unused release carried forward; stock-adding join = built - requirement | every vacant dwelling usable where needed, reallocated from 1 January 2027 | v = 0; absorption 1 | DECISION (author): theoretical limit of L2a / L2b | DECISION |
| T2 No extra space | L1 with f = 1: size = occupied area S(t) x OLF (T3's OLF) (`size`) | no space above the occupied area | f = 1 (2050 size 52.2 m2 with T3) | DECISION (author): theoretical limit of L1 | DECISION |
| T3 Minimum space per person | OLF of every new building = the lowest design OLF (GFA / design occupants) of the independent case studies (`olf`, all typologies) | an apartment-block occupancy applied to every typology | 19.69 m2/person (A_1); replaces Detached 36.46, Townhouses 33.11, Apartments 20.63 | DATA: Christoforatos G, Pickering K (2025) Smart and Sustainable Built Environment, doi:10.1108/SASBE-06-2025-0304 (data/building_data.xlsx; duplicate A_2 excluded) | DATA |
| T4 Best materials | each typology's A1-A3 per m2 at its own best independent case, on top of decarbonisation (as L5) | the best observed design of each typology built everywhere | Detached r = 0.530 (SD_2), Townhouses r = 0.880 (T_2), Apartments r = 1.000 (held: one independent case) | DATA: case studies (outputs/factors/factors_building.csv, 2025 factors) | DATA |
| T5 Best soil | soil factor at the lowest soil order (SOC_low), applied exactly through the soil-bearing share | the lowest of 10 soil orders under every new footprint | Detached 22.9 (vs 50.1), Townhouses 13.8 (vs 30.3), Apartments 2.5 (vs 5.5) kg CO2e/m2 | DATA: Christoforatos G, Pickering K, Schipper LA (2026) Journal of Environmental Management 415, 130603 (the existing lower-bound sensitivity) | DATA |
| T6 Urban densification | a share s of each year's non-replacement new floor area 2027-2050 is on previously developed land (zero soil); the rest carries the T5 factor: soil factor x (1 - s) on the soil-bearing floor area | (i) Auckland's observed share applied nationally (demonstrated-limit logic, as T3 / T4); (ii) a dwelling-count share applied to floor area; (iii) intensification on developed land seals no additional soil (upper bound: some infill builds over garden soil); (iv) replacement floor area keeps its existing zero-soil treatment; (v) the soil factor on the remaining share is T5's lowest soil order | s = 0.82 x 0.79 = 0.648, rounded 0.65 | DATA: Auckland Council (2021). Auckland Plan 2050 Development Strategy Monitoring Report, December 2021: in 2020/21, 82% of dwelling consents were in the existing urban area, of which 79% occurred through intensification (Auckland monitoring); DECISION (author): national application | DATA + DECISION |

Table note: T is a hyper-optimistic theoretical limit (thought experiment): all assumptions at full strength from 1 January 2027, combining best observed attributes of different buildings and places; not a proposal or a feasible pathway (potentials hierarchy: theoretical > technical > realisable).

**Banking rule (T1).** raw_t = requirement_t + absorbed near-term excess_t (negative when the release of vacant or surplus dwellings exceeds the year's need); D_t = raw_t − bank_(t−1); built_t = max(0, D_t); bank_t = max(0, −D_t). The banked path enters engine.forward as a stock-adding join, join_t = built_t − requirement_t (join_redev = 0), so the stock identity holds and implied vacancy = stock_join / (households + stock_join) ≥ 0. Banked zero-building years carry floating-point noise of about 1e-12 dwellings; the checks use 1e-6 dwellings. The banking rule is applied in every T-family run (it binds only where the release exceeds the need).

**Soil path (T5, T6).** The engine takes one soil factor per typology; the year-dependent factor is applied exactly by replacing the engine soil term in the intensity: I'(y) = I(y) − SOC_avg · share(y) + SOC_path(y) · share(y), with share(y) the soil-bearing (non-replacement) share of the floor area built in year y, taken from the engine and independent of the intensity (identical in both passes; tested). T5: SOC_path = SOC_low. T6: SOC_path(y) = SOC_T5(y) · (1 − s w(y)), s = 0.82 × 0.79 = 0.648, rounded 0.65, i.e. a share s of each year's non-replacement floor area carries zero soil and the rest the T5 factor (tested to 1e-9). The engine share is 1 − soil-free / total floor area; in banked years with no new building (total ≈ 0, floating-point noise) it is undefined, so share(y) is clipped to [0, 1] and set to 0 where the floor area built is ≤ 1e-3 m². In v3 the unclipped share entered with a negative sign in those years and understated T's soil carbon by 5.5 kt (corrected in v3.1).

**T6 source and assumptions.** Auckland Council (2021). Auckland Plan 2050 Development Strategy Monitoring Report, December 2021: in 2020/21, 82% of dwelling consents were in the existing urban area, of which 79% occurred through intensification. Assumptions: (i) Auckland's observed share applied nationally (demonstrated-limit logic, as T3 / T4); (ii) a dwelling-count share applied to floor area; (iii) intensification on developed land seals no additional soil (upper bound: some infill builds over garden soil); (iv) replacement floor area keeps its existing zero-soil treatment; (v) the soil factor on the remaining share is T5's lowest soil order. Tag: DATA (the Auckland shares) + DECISION (author: their national application to floor area).

AtP: T 4.11; the minimum attainable (2026 cohort alone) is 1.28, so AtP is not attainable within the window.

### Limitations of T

* T combines attributes of different buildings and places (the OLF of A_1, an apartment block, applied to every typology; each typology's best A1-A3 case; the lowest soil order everywhere; Auckland's 2020/21 intensification share nationally) that have not been observed together; it is a hyper-optimistic thought experiment, not a design, a policy or a feasible pathway.
* T2 + T3 give every new dwelling the occupied area of the case-study minimum (about 20 m² per person); no design rule, accessibility standard or household-size variation is modelled.
* T1 assumes every vacant dwelling is usable where it is needed (no spatial or condition mismatch; Napiontek et al. 2025 on hibernating stock) and an instant reallocation in 2027.
* T6 is an upper bound on the soil saving (assumption iii: some infill builds over garden soil) and transfers a dwelling-count share of one city to national floor area; its benefits beyond soil (infrastructure, transport energy) are outside the embodied-carbon scope, as for the removed L4.
* As in P1-P5, the renovation carbon of the kept stock (L3) and any rebound are not modelled; deterministic, median demographics; static budgets.
